# action.docker_swarm_rotate_ca

<!-- Code generated by tools/genskill from the provider schema. DO NOT EDIT. -->

Kind: action. Back to [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md).

Rotates the swarm root CA, like `docker swarm ca --rotate`: a new self-signed root, or the given signing certificate and key (`Spec.CAConfig.SigningCACert` / `SigningCAKey`), with `CAConfig.ForceRotate` incremented. Every node gets a certificate from the new root. The provider's host must be a manager. The result object has the new `tls_info` and whether the root rotation is still in progress.

Actions need Terraform >= 1.14. They keep no state: they run when a
resource's `lifecycle { action_trigger { ... } }` fires, or on demand with
`terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_swarm_rotate_ca.<name>`. Arguments go inside
the action's `config` block.

## Usage

```terraform
action "docker_swarm_rotate_ca" "<name>" {
  config {
    # arguments below
  }
}

# Run it: lifecycle { action_trigger { events = [after_create] actions = [action.docker_swarm_rotate_ca.<name>] } }
# on a resource, or: terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_swarm_rotate_ca.<name>
```

## Arguments and attributes

| Name | Type | Status | Forces replacement | Sensitive | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `result_path` | `string` | optional |  |  | Local file the action writes its result object to after a successful run. The file holds one JSON object keyed by the action's output names (`result`, the identity values, the raw outputs with their `*_sha256` hashes, and the version values), with keys sorted at every level, two-space indentation and a trailing newline; it is written atomically (temporary file, then rename) and parent directories are created. Read it in a later run with `jsondecode(file(...))` or the `local_file` data source. Sensitive values are written in full, since this is your own file, but show as `(sensitive)` in the progress message. Nothing is written when the action fails. |
| `signing_ca_cert` | `string` | optional |  |  | PEM root CA certificate to rotate to (`SigningCACert`). Requires `signing_ca_key`. Unset generates a new root. |
| `signing_ca_key` | `string` | optional |  |  | PEM private key of `signing_ca_cert` (`SigningCAKey`). Actions keep no state, so the key is only sent to the Engine; it is never returned by the Engine or written to the progress messages or the result. |
| `timeout` | `string` | optional |  |  | How long to wait, as a Go duration. Default `10m`. |
| `wait` | `bool` | optional |  |  | Wait until the root rotation has finished on every node. Default `true`. |

## Example

```terraform
resource "terraform_data" "ca_rotation" {
  # Bump to rotate the swarm root CA again.
  input = 1

  lifecycle {
    action_trigger {
      events  = [after_create, after_update]
      actions = [action.docker_swarm_rotate_ca.yearly]
    }
  }
}

# Rotates to a new self-signed root CA and waits until every node has a
# certificate from it. On demand:
#   terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_swarm_rotate_ca.yearly
action "docker_swarm_rotate_ca" "yearly" {
  config {
    timeout     = "15m"
    result_path = "${path.module}/ca-rotation.json"
  }
}
```
